clue.text: Keeping quiet, having doubt

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
a reservation is a doubt or misgiving

explanation.surface: Someone keeps their mouth shut because they have misgivings.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping something is maintaining it intact, which is what conservation or upkeep of it amounts to.

clue.text: Knock up competent story

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for knock is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rap is a knock
able means competent

explanation.surface: A skilled writer quickly knocks together a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock up' poses as one phrase meaning to throw together; split it, and 'up' is the reversal signal in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A parable is a short moral tale, a kind of story.

clue.text: Unsatisfying not to get a start in US. though keen

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter, since it is denied a start

parts.note: meager, the American spelling of meagre, means scanty and unsatisfying

explanation.surface: Something in America is disappointing, but people are keen on it all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in US.' tells you to use the American spelling MEAGER rather than British MEAGRE; dropping its first letter leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager and keen are synonyms for being enthusiastic.

clue.text: Advanced to capture home with serious intent

indicators.note: one word takes another prisoner inside it

parts.note: early means advanced, ahead of time
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Troops press forward to seize a dwelling in deadly earnest.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something earnestly means doing it sincerely and in all seriousness.

clue.text: One in front, strutting

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the van is the front, as in vanguard
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone at the head of the line struts about.
explanation.definitionFit: Strutting suggests conceit, and a vain person is conceited.

clue.text: Follow note in Philippine language

indicators.note: the single letter is placed within the language name

parts.note: Tagalog is the main language of the Philippines
n is the abbreviation for note, as in a footnote reference

explanation.surface: Read a footnote written in Tagalog.
explanation.definitionFit: To tag along is to follow someone, often uninvited.

clue.text: Rough time? Nothing in it

indicators.note: the answer sits inside these two words, run together

explanation.surface: Having a hard time? There's nothing to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ought is a dialect or old variant of nought, meaning zero.

clue.text: Roundabout where vehicle runs over bird

indicators.note: in a down clue, one word sits above and on top of the other

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
ousel, or ouzel, is a blackbird or similar bird

explanation.surface: A car hits a bird at a traffic roundabout.
explanation.walkthrough: A roundabout here is the fairground ride, not the road junction the surface pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A carousel is a merry-go-round, called a roundabout in Britain.

clue.text: Old lovers race home

explanation.surface: Former sweethearts dash back to their house.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemans are archaic sweethearts; the French town Le Mans hosts the famous 24-hour motor race.

clue.text: About to call doctor — get on back inside

indicators.note: the reversed run goes within the word for phoning

parts.note: to ring is to call on the telephone

indicators.note: the two pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: to age is to get on in years

explanation.surface: Someone is about to phone the doctor, then retreat indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DRAGE into EGARD, which goes inside RING.
explanation.definitionFit: Regarding is a preposition meaning concerning or on the subject of.

clue.text: Serious shortage of Bordeaux wine

indicators.note: the wine name is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Graves is a wine from the Bordeaux region

explanation.surface: A sommelier is troubled by a scarcity of claret.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave and serious both describe something solemn or weighty.

clue.text: Carried round island

parts.note: borne is the past participle of bear, to carry
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone was carried around an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Borneo is a large island in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Excess prayer engulfing god

indicators.note: the first word swallows the second inside it

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request, a prayer
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: Too much praying swamps the deity.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an overabundance, too much of something.

clue.text: Worth of house quietly reviewed, after losing money

indicators.note: the letters are looked over again and rearranged

parts.note: L is the pound sign, standing for money

explanation.surface: A house is quietly revalued after its owner loses cash.
explanation.walkthrough: QUIETLY rearranged holds the answer plus L; 'after losing' tells you the L comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity is the value of a property beyond what is owed on it.

clue.text: Statesman as initial alternative for government

definitions.text: Statesman as initial alternative for government

parts.words: Statesman as initial alternative for government
parts.note: read Statesman as States man: the figure whose initials are the same as those of the United States, used as a stand-in for its government

explanation.surface: A politician acts as an early substitute for those in power.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded figure in a top hat personifies the US government.

clue.text: Gossip the foundation for Xenophon's work?

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or gossip about a person
a basis is a foundation

explanation.surface: Chit-chat is the groundwork for an ancient Greek writer's book.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anabasis is Xenophon's account of the Greek mercenaries' march into Persia.

clue.text: Hit the water here on the Thames

parts.note: to batter is to hit repeatedly
the sea is a body of water

explanation.surface: Someone strikes the river at a spot on the Thames.
explanation.walkthrough: BATTERSEA is a district of south London on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Battersea is a London district on the south bank of the river, its power station a landmark.

clue.text: Region in which a couple of partners perform

indicators.note: the region holds the following pieces within it

parts.note: a tract is an area or region
N and S, North and South, are a partnership at bridge

explanation.surface: In a certain area, two partners put on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: At bridge, North and South play as partners, so NS is a pair of partners.
explanation.definitionFit: To transact business is to carry it out or perform it.

clue.text: Dray put in area behind house

parts.note: the clue word is what you get by writing the word for an enclosed area backwards

explanation.surface: A horse-drawn cart is parked in the garden behind a home.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as an instruction, the answer says to put YARD back to front, which spells DRAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A backyard is the garden or enclosed ground at the rear of a house.

clue.text: Be about to offer a mineral

indicators.note: the first word goes around the second

parts.note: to lend is to give or offer temporarily

explanation.surface: Someone is about to present a rock specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be about to' poses as one phrase meaning 'be on the point of'; split it, and 'about' is the container signal while 'to offer' is the inner piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Blende is a zinc sulphide ore, a mineral also called sphalerite.

clue.text: Prison has a convict on the way

indicators.note: in an across clue, the phrase following comes after the road word

parts.note: ST is street, a way
lag is slang for a convict, as in old lag

explanation.surface: A jail holds an inmate on his way somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: A stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalag is a German prisoner-of-war camp, so a kind of prison.

clue.text: Opera composer not quite taken in by pig of a librettist

indicators.note: the shortened composer is held inside the word for pig

parts.note: a gilt is a young sow

indicators.note: the composer's name falls short by its last letter

parts.note: Alban Berg composed the operas Wozzeck and Lulu

explanation.surface: An opera composer is somewhat fooled by a boorish lyric writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pig of a librettist' poses as an insult, but 'pig' is a young sow and 'of a' is only a link; 'not quite' trims the composer and 'taken in by' places him.
explanation.definitionFit: W. S. Gilbert wrote the words for Sullivan's comic operas.

clue.text: The plane could be a jumbo

indicators.note: these letters could be rearranged to form something else

explanation.surface: The aircraft might be a jumbo jet.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumbo suggests the jet, but Jumbo was a famous large animal at London Zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo is a common nickname for a large tusked animal, after the famous zoo specimen.

clue.text: Cut and share round

explanation.surface: Slash the budget and spread it out.
explanation.definitionFit: To halve is to cut in two, and to split something into two equal shares.

clue.text: Selected soldiers in dock?

explanation.surface: A chosen squad waits at the quayside.
explanation.walkthrough: A detail is a small group picked for a duty; read the answer as de-tail, to dock an animal's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A detail is a party chosen for a task; docking removes a tail.

clue.text: Saw a defunct oath resurrected

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: egad is an old-fashioned exclamation

explanation.surface: Someone witnessed an extinct curse come back to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see, but it is the noun meaning a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying, a proverb.

clue.text: Members needed by gun club

explanation.surface: Members are required by a shooting society.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms are limbs, members of the body; arms are also weapons, such as guns and clubs.

clue.text: Randomly choose length of extended speech

parts.note: to draw lots is to choose at random

explanation.surface: Pick at random how long a long speech should be.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is slow speech with drawn-out vowels.

clue.text: Love getting in quickly to build hi-tech industry

indicators.note: one word gets inside the other

parts.note: apace means quickly
Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: Romance hurriedly enters to create an advanced manufacturing sector.
explanation.definitionFit: The aerospace industry builds aircraft and spacecraft, at the frontier of technology.

clue.text: Novel will complete book collection

parts.note: novel means new
a last will and testament

explanation.surface: A newly written will finishes off someone's library.
explanation.definitionFit: The latter part of the Bible is a collection of twenty-seven books.
